summary: A Baldwin County grand jury indicted Orange Beach business owners John and Angel McNider on elder financial-exploitation and theft charges, FOX10 reported. Fairhope police are investigating a possible drowning after a man was found dead near a pier, and the jail booked 10 people on criminal charges dated Wednesday, including a sheriff's domestic-violence arrest.

entries.title: Indicted, elder financial exploitation: John McNider, Angel McNider
body: A Baldwin County grand jury has indicted John McNider, 56, and Angel McNider, 54, owners of an Orange Beach boat-lift business, on a combined eight counts of financial exploitation of the elderly, FOX10 reported Thursday, citing court documents filed this week. The station said the documents name six alleged victims and put the value in each case above $2,500.

FOX10 reported that John McNider also faces two counts of first-degree theft of property and Angel McNider one, and that both face an electronic stalking charge. Angel McNider's attorney told the station she has not spoken to the person named in that charge in three years. Both were released from the county jail; their arraignment is set for Jan. 20, the station reported.

entries.title: Domestic violence arrest: Ramero Deaundre Perdue
body: Ramero Deaundre Perdue, 38, was arrested by the Baldwin County Sheriff's Office at 4:05 p.m. Wednesday, Nov. 11, according to the jail roster. No sheriff's office statement or news report was found.

The roster lists three counts of third-degree domestic violence — an assault, harassment or similar offence against a family or household member — along with third-degree criminal trespass and a third-degree assault/criminal mischief charge. He was in custody when the roster was read early Thursday.

entries.title: Death investigation: man found in water near Fairhope pier
body: Fairhope police said officers responded to a 911 call at about 7:45 a.m. Wednesday, Nov. 11, and found a man dead in the water near a private pier on Sea Cliff Drive, FOX10 and WKRG reported. Police are investigating the death as a possible drowning.
Police said there was no indication of foul play. The man had not been identified publicly pending notification of his family.

entries.title: Other arrests Nov. 10–11: Kelvin Quantavious Culbreath, Brandon Allan Card, James Percy Blair II, Aynsleigh Nicole Aspen Howard
body: Foley police arrested Kelvin Quantavious Culbreath, 23, at 1:54 a.m. Wednesday, Nov. 11, and booked him on charges of possessing dangerous drugs and second-degree marijuana possession; he was in custody. Foley police also arrested Brandon Allan Card, 44, at 9:16 p.m. Tuesday, Nov. 10, on two counts of possessing dangerous drugs, marijuana possession and drug paraphernalia; the roster shows him released Nov. 11.

James Percy Blair II, 43, arrested by Daphne police Nov. 10, was booked into the county jail Nov. 11 on a charge of promoting prison contraband involving drugs — bringing drugs into a jail. Aynsleigh Nicole Aspen Howard, 21, was arrested by the sheriff's office at 12:42 a.m. Nov. 11 and booked on a charge of harassing a family member. Both were in custody. All information is from the jail roster.

entries.title: Life without parole: Joseph Kaynen Gurley
body: Joseph Kaynen Gurley, 26, was sentenced Tuesday, Nov. 10, to life in prison without the possibility of parole on his murder and attempted murder convictions, WKRG reported; the Baldwin County District Attorney's office updated its Aug. 20 post to say he received life without parole. FOX10 reported two life sentences.

A Baldwin County jury convicted Gurley in August after a four-day trial in a shooting on March 31, 2024, at an apartment complex off County Road 64 in Daphne that killed one man and wounded another, according to the District Attorney's office. Prosecutor Patrick Doggett tried the case; Daphne police investigated.

entries.title: Terrorist-threat arrest near Foley schools: Gregory McGowen
body: Foley police said officers were called at about 7:40 a.m. Tuesday, Nov. 10, to a report of a man with a gun near 9th Avenue and South Oak Street, close to two Foley schools, which secured their buildings. Police said Gregory McGowen, 59, of Foley, had no weapon on him when officers made contact; a replica firearm, which police said was a BB gun, was recovered a short distance away, WKRG reported.

Police said he was first charged with menacing, which they described as a Class B misdemeanor, and that the charge was upgraded to making a terrorist threat in the first degree, which police described as a Class B felony, because of the disruption at the schools. Alabama law allows 2 to 20 years for a Class B felony. The jail roster lists him booked by Foley police Nov. 10 on the terrorist-threat charge and an aggravated assault/menacing charge with a weapon; he was in custody when the roster was read early Thursday.

entries.title: Teen shot in vehicle: Foley police investigating
body: Foley police said they received a report at about 2:45 a.m. Tuesday, Nov. 10, of a 16-year-old with a gunshot wound. Police said three juveniles were riding in a car near North Pine Street when a gun went off and struck the teen in the torso, WKRG reported. The teen was treated at a hospital and was in stable condition.

Investigators said they believe the shooting was accidental, have identified and interviewed everyone involved, and do not believe there is a threat to the public. Police said criminal charges are possible. No one has been named.

entries.title: Child abuse arrest: Kameron J. Jackson
body: Kameron J. Jackson, 19, was booked into the Baldwin County jail Tuesday, Nov. 10, on an arrest by Robertsdale police dated Nov. 9, according to the jail roster. No police statement or news report was found.

The roster lists one booked charge, torture or willful abuse of a child, in the family category — a charge of deliberately abusing or cruelly mistreating a child. He was in custody when the roster was read early Thursday.

entries.title: Obscene material arrest: Michael Ryan Cain
body: Michael Ryan Cain, 22, was arrested by the Baldwin County Sheriff's Office at 12:06 p.m. Tuesday, Nov. 10, according to the jail roster. No sheriff's office statement or news report was found.
The roster lists two booked counts of distributing obscene material — a charge of distributing material the law defines as obscene. He was in custody when the roster was read early Thursday.

entries.title: Other arrests Nov. 9–10: Christal Irene Pryear, Bradley Terrell Heard, Shawn Derek Wilson, Erick Stromas
body: Christal Irene Pryear, 31, was arrested by Orange Beach police at 9:42 p.m. Monday, Nov. 9, and booked on charges of attempting to elude a police officer and second-degree marijuana possession; the roster shows her released Nov. 11. Bradley Terrell Heard, 33, was arrested by Gulf Shores police Nov. 9 and booked on a charge of receiving a stolen vehicle; the roster shows him released Nov. 10.

Shawn Derek Wilson, 39, was arrested by the sheriff's office at 9:22 p.m. Tuesday, Nov. 10, and booked on charges of harassment of a family member and obstructing governmental operations; the roster shows him released Nov. 11. Erick Stromas, 19, was arrested by Gulf Shores police Nov. 10 and booked as a fugitive from justice — held on a warrant from another state or jurisdiction; he was in custody. All information is from the jail roster.
